about: Which GPU runs which model, and how. scripts/recipe.py turns a recipe id into the environment scripts/up.sh launches with; the frontend lists what is here. Every number carries {v, measured, src}: measured means read on that card, anything else is an estimate and says so.

cu_per_hour.src: Colab /tun/m/ccu-info consumptionRateHourly with this box as the account's only assignment, 2026-09-25 (older docs quote 7.52)
Colab UI figure, never read from ccu-info

vram.src: a 40 GB draw probes at ~39 GiB (scripts/restore.py)

ram.src: Colab's standard A100 shape; not probed here

prefill_tps.src: gcs sweep at 8192, docs/MEASURED.md (2,806 at gcs 2048)

decode_tps.src: MTP ndt 4 at a 30K context, docs/MEASURED.md

eta_min.src: download 280 s + load 259.5 s + install, docs/MEASURED.md

vram_mib.src: after load at cache 500224, gcs 4096, vision off; with gcs 8192 and the tower together: not measured

context.src: the KV fits (measured); positions past the native 262,144 come from YaRN x2 (rope_parameters + max_position_embeddings 524288, which is how exllamav3 derives the factor); quality there not measured

vision.src: the pack carries vision_k6.safetensors (561 MB); its weights sit in pinned host RAM (EXL3_VISION_PINNED) so the tower costs no VRAM for weights; image encoding speed not measured

concurrency.src: api_server serialises requests; how many live jobs would fit is computed in docs/CONCURRENCY.md, never exercised

weights.src: 15,362,272,350 B at branch 3.50bpw (Hugging Face tree), vision tower and MTP layer included

vram_mib.src: derived: 14.3 GiB weights + ~4.5 GiB Q4 KV at 262K (16 full-attention layers x 4 KV heads x 256) + recurrent state + staging; never loaded

eta_min.src: 15.4 GB download (~40 s at the 380 MB/s seen for the 80G pack) + install + load, never timed

context.src: native max_position_embeddings; no YaRN in this recipe

vision.src: the tower is bf16 inside the shards (preprocessor_config.json present); never loaded

host_ram.src: no n-gram table in this pack, so the 83 GB shape has room
